transcript.text: There's water all over the kitchen floor coming from under my Beko washing machine and its gone under the units to where the plug is, the machine is still going. What do I do?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. Do not touch any wet plugs or switches with wet hands; if you cannot reach the plug safely due to the water, turn off the electricity at the fuse box instead. Once the power is isolated, we can look for the source of the leak. Common causes include a blocked drain filter, a loose hose, or a worn door seal.
I'm standing in the water in my socks right now, is that ok?? The fuse box is in the hall and the floor's dry there, so I can get to it. Should I switch off the whole thing?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
No, it is not safe to stand in water with electricity nearby. Please go to the fuse box now and switch off the main power supply immediately. Do not touch the washing machine or any wet plugs until you have done this.
ok I'm going to the fuse box now. The water has run back towards the socket under the worktop and the floor under the plug is wet. Do I switch off just the main switch?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Yes, please switch off the main isolator switch at the fuse box right now to cut all power to the kitchen. This is critical because water and electricity are a lethal combination, especially with water near your plug socket. Do not touch any wet plugs or switches yourself; use the dry switch in the hall. Once the power is isolated, we can safely investigate the leak.
ok I'm at the fuse box, switching the main switch off now. Ok it's off. What do I do next about the leak? the machine was still full of water

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Good job getting the power off; that keeps everyone safe. Please place some old towels on the floor in front of the machine to catch any spillage. Open the small access flap at the bottom front (usually left-hand side). Pull out the drain filter slowly into a shallow tray or bowl to let the water drip out, then unscrew it fully. Check if the filter is clogged with debris (like coins, lint, or hair) and see if the plastic impeller inside spins freely by hand. Let me know what you find.
ok the drain filter flap is tight and the area behind it is dry. the water is mostly coming from the front under the door though. what else should I check?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Since the drain filter area is dry but water is coming from under the door, the leak is likely originating from the door seal (boot) or an internal hose near that area. The most common cause here is a foreign object (like a coin or bra wire) stuck in the seal causing it to leak, or a tear in the rubber itself. Please pull back the folds of the rubber door seal at the front and check for any debris caught inside, and inspect the rubber for tears. Let me know what you find.
ok I looked at the door seal, theres a small split in the rubber at the bottom fold and a bra underwire stuck right next to it. is that the cause? what do I do now?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Yes, that is definitely the cause. The underwire has punctured the rubber seal, and water is leaking out through that split. 1. Remove the bra underwire carefully.
2. Because the seal is torn, it will continue to leak even if you remove the wire. You will need to replace the door seal (also called a door boot). This involves removing the old seal and fitting a new one; it usually requires some basic tools like a screwdriver or pliers to release the retaining spring/wire.
3. Before buying parts, check your Beko model number (usually on a sticker inside the door frame) to ensure you get the correct replacement seal. If you are not comfortable dismantling the front of the machine to replace the seal, please call an appliance engineer to do it for you.
